statement: Using events.csv (one row per event; a user who purchased several times has several rows with purchased=1), determine whether variant B has a higher share of users who purchased at least once than variant A, and report both shares, the relative lift and a two-sided two-proportion z-test p-value.
success_criterion: The reported shares, lift and p-value are the correct per-user figures for this data, and the conclusion follows from them.
oracles: recompute the shares independently from events.csv

submission.claim: Variant B has a higher share of purchasing users than A: 13.0% against 9.8%, a relative lift of about +32% (two-sided z-test p = 0.0001).
assertions: 295 of 3000 users in A purchased at least once (9.8%)
390 of 3000 users in B purchased at least once (13.0%)
the relative lift of B over A is +32.2%
the difference is statistically significant at the 5% level (p = 0.0001)
submission.provenance: analysis.py reads events.csv with the csv module, collects the set of users and the set of purchasing users per variant, and runs a pooled two-proportion z-test. Output saved to output.txt.
